summary: Lookout site since as early as 1907 (emergency lookout from 1915) on a Klamath County peak; the 30 ft R-6 tower (dated 1961 or 1963) still stands, staffed in summer, behind a vehicle gate.

facts.design: R-6 live-in flattop cab with catwalk on a 30 ft treated wood tower

staffing.status: staffed in summer (firelookout.com: staffed every summer; 2013 and 2024 visitor reports)

access.note: Public motor vehicles are prohibited beyond a gate on the road. Visitors walk about 0.8 mile from the gate. The tower is an active, staffed lookout.

visit.trail_note: Road 5815 leads from Highway 58 to Road 500. Park at the gated switchback, then walk the 0.8 mile road to the summit.

events.note: Used as a patrol lookout as early as 1907, per the Register.
Established as an emergency lookout in 1915. A July 1915 ranger visit to the summit weighed a lookout station.
Frame cabin on a log crib. Dates disputed: the Register dates the crib to the 1920s; firelookout.com and a 2013 blog say 1916.
A newspaper item reported a lightning fire on Odell Butte in July 1927. A temporary lookout was stationed there that August.
An L-4 cab on a 20 ft tower replaced the earlier cabin.
The lookout was on the Crescent district roster for 1942. In October a district guard closed the station for the winter.
The Register gives 1961 for the 30 ft tower with R-6 cab.
firelookout.com and a 2013 blog give 1963 for the same 30 ft tower with R-6 cab.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on March 1, 2003.
A June 2024 visitor was invited up the tower and spoke with the lookout.

corrections.why: The 6.1 m (20 ft) in the record describes the earlier L-4 tower. The R-6 tower standing today is 30 ft, per the Register (30' treated wood tower) and firelookout.com (30' treated timber tower).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 1961; firelookout.com and a 2013 blog give 1963. An April 1962 Bend Bulletin item had planned a 20 ft tower. The record keeps the Register's 1961, and the story gives both dates. No source explains the change to 30 ft.
The Register dates the log crib to the 1920s and the cabin to 12 by 12 ft; firelookout.com says 1916 and 12x12 ft; a 2013 blog says 1916 and 14 by 14 ft. The story leaves this open.
The Register gives 6,931 ft (2,113 m); firelookout.com and the 2013 and 2024 blogs give 7,033 ft. The record's 2112.6 m matches the Register.

Firelookout.com says about 8 miles east of Crescent; the 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note reproduced on Oregon Lookouts says about 9 miles west. The story gives both; no source read resolves the direction.

notes_for_editor: Staffing and the current tower date rest on visitor blogs and an undated firelookout.com page. The 1915, 1927, 1942 and 1962 newspaper items are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. No Forest Service or Deschutes National Forest page was read. Photos not added: firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber, but no image URLs or licenses were confirmed.
